To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Drosophila larval fat body is an organ with a complex cellular structure that undergoes dramatic changes during development, and that these cellular changes correlate with the accumulation of storage substances in the fat body cells.

(1) the formation of fatty bodies in the larvae of D. melanogaster involves the formation of a large number of small droplets, which then coalesce to form a single large droplet, (2) this process is accompanied by changes in the size, shape, and internal structure of the fat cells, and (3) these changes are associated with the formation of a number of organelles, which are involved in lipid synthesis, lipid transport, and energy production.
the Drosophila larval fat body is a dynamic and plastic organ that undergoes a series of morphological and biochemical changes during development.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a study of variation in the size of cell organelles during the formation of reserve substances in the fatty body of the larva.
the development of an integrated approach to the study of the structure of a protein and of its function.

the study of the variation in the number of mitochondria, ribosomes, and lipid droplets in the fat body cells of Drosophila larvae during the period of the formation of reserve substances in the fat body.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the formation of the fat body in D. melanogaster is a process of cell differentiation and cell proliferation.

in the course of the larval development of Drosophila the cell organelles of the fat body are subject to a series of variations in size and number which are correlated with the synthesis and storage of the different reserve substances.

the formation and the growth of the fat body of the Drosophila larva is characterized by a great number of changes and modifications of the cell organelles, which are not only of morphological nature, but also of biochemical nature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the formation of the larval fat body of Drosophila is characterized by a series of changes in the cell organelles, especially in the mitochondria, endoplasmic reticulum and ribosomes.
we have shown that there are no differences in the number of mitochondria, lipid droplets or ribosomes between the two cell types.
the larval fat bodies are a dynamic organ in terms of cell organelles, which are involved in the storage of reserve substances.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the cell cycle and the circadian clock are not as separate as once believed.
the cell organelles are not fixed in their structure and composition.
the cell cycle is an important regulator of lipid metabolism in Drosophila, and that this regulation is mediated through TORC1 and TORC2.
